turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he was not threatening him with fear, but with the reality of the situation, and that the oppression of his tenantry had to end, and that he would not tolerate it any longer.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil that he was wasting his breath on threats, that his own estates were prospering while Nikhil's were on the brink of collapse, and that he should focus on his own problems rather than spreading baseless accusations.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he found it unfortunate that Sandip would rather mock the situation than acknowledge the truth and that his own prosperity was built on the suffering of others.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil that he was still waiting for some concrete evidence of these 'sufferings' of Nikhil's tenantry, and that until then, his boasts and accusations sounded like the empty threats of a bankrupt zamindar.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil insisted that Sandip was willfully blind to the plight of his own tenantry, and that he should be ashamed of his own role in perpetuating their suffering.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip asked Nikhil with a smirk, 'Is this the sort of high-mindedness that passes for politics in these parts?', 'what, Nikhil, a social reformer now?'

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil warned Sandip that his flippant attitude was a dereliction of duty, and that as a zamindar, it was his responsibility to acknowledge and address the suffering of his tenantry, not mock it.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip asked Bimala, with a mischievous glance at Nikhil, whether it was time for her to remind Nikhil of his own family's history of exploiting the poor.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Sandip, with a calm and inquiring expression, whether his concerns about Nikhil's motives were not, in fact, a distraction from the real issue at hand.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip chuckled and said that Nikhil's sudden concern for the tenantry's rights was quaint, implying that he had been playing the role of a guardian all along, while Sandip was the villain who had been exploiting them.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that his flippant attitude was a testament to his own lack of vision, and that he would not stand idly by while the tenantry suffered.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip shot back at Nikhil, laughing and saying that the idea of him being a guardian of the tenantry was almost too rich to bear.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil warned Sandip that his careless words and actions would only serve to embolden the Mussulmans and exacerbate the tensions in the region

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Nikhil whether his warnings of potential attacks had been preceded by any concrete evidence, and what specific measures he proposed to mitigate the situation.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he would not be swayed by Sandip's flippant nature, and that the gravity of the situation demanded a serious and measured response.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil that his warnings were nothing but a thinly veiled attempt to undermine his own position as a zamindar, and that he wouldn't fall for such petty politics.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil insisted that the safety of the tenantry was his paramount concern, and he would not be swayed by petty squabbles over status and position.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Sandip whether he had considered the potential consequences of his actions on the relationships between the zamindar and the local Mussulmans.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil pointed out that the zamindars' duties went beyond mere politics and that they had a responsibility to protect their people and maintain order in the region

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip retorted that Nikhil's warnings were as timely as a monsoon rain in a parched landscape, and that he had more pressing concerns than the whims of local Mussulmans.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Bimala where she would go, addressing her as the Queen.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he kept Browning among his books, reminding him of a contest they had over translating lines from Browning, and inquiring if Nikhil remembered it.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil and Bimala that he had managed to translate the lines into Bengali, but the result was unlikely to be well-received, and that he had once thought he was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence had intervened to prevent it, and he recalled old Dakshina's poetry.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Bimala that it was pointless to search the bookshelves, as Nikhil no longer read poetry since his marriage, but that he, Sandip, was about to be afflicted with the 'fever fit of poesy' again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil warned Sandip that he had come to give him a warning.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was warning him about the 'fever fit of poesy'.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that for some time, Mahomedan preachers had been stirring up the local Mussulmans, who were angry with Sandip and might attack him at any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he had come to advise him to flee.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had come to give him information, not advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil that if the estates were his, a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for him, and that Nikhil should intimidate the preachers instead of frightening him, and that Nikhil's weakness was also affecting his neighbouring zamindars.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had not offered him advice, and that he wished Sandip would refrain from giving him his advice, as it was useless, and that there was another thing he wanted to tell Sandip, namely that Sandip and his followers had been secretly oppressing Nikhil's tenantry, and that he could no longer allow that, so he must ask Sandip to leave his territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was threatening him with fear of the Mussulmans, or if there was another fear he had to threaten him with.
